evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: `export function createApp(): Express` creates the Catalogue, OrderService and CatalogueService, then registers the /products and /orders routes. All of it serves the HTTP API.
src/infrastructure/index.ts: calls `createApp()` and `app.listen(PORT, ...)` to start the server and nothing else.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: every handler goes through `catalogueService.*` or `orderService.*`, so the module's service abstractions are used consistently.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: the same catch block (`error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'` with `res.status(400)`) appears in the POST /orders, PATCH /orders/:orderId/state and POST /orders/:orderId/cancel handlers. This is minor repeated boilerplate.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: `orderService.getOrdersByState(state as any)` uses a type cast instead of validating the state value. It gets around a type from another layer, not this module's own abstraction.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: `catalogueService.addProduct('PROD001', ...)` loads sample data inside the app factory.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit passes. Both files serve one concern: delivering the order-fulfilment HTTP API. app.ts builds the Express app, wires up the services and defines the routes. index.ts starts the server and does nothing else. All route handlers go through the services (CatalogueService and OrderService) and never touch domain state directly, so they use the module's abstractions consistently. The split between the two files is clean.

I found a few minor issues, but none rises to a cohesion failure:
- The same catch block, `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'` followed by `res.status(400)`, is repeated in three handlers. This is repeated boilerplate rather than a duplicated business rule.
- The POST /orders handler checks that the items array is not empty. The domain or application layer may enforce the same rule, but I can't see that code, so I can't confirm a duplicated invariant.
- In GET /orders, `state as any` gets around the application layer's own state type. It does not get around anything this module defines.
- Sample catalogue data is loaded inside createApp. This mixes test-data setup into the app factory, but it is still part of composing the app.
